## Tips

I have some of my own:

::: {.callout-tip}
If I get an error like this:

```text
Error running filter /Applications/quarto/share/filters/main.lua:
/Applications/quarto/share/filters/main.lua:2479: attempt to index a nil value (local 'el')
```

It means I had a `.qmd` file containing a plain markdown link with empty text, e.g.

```markdown
[](https://github.com)
```

This is valid markdown but not valid Quarto.
:::

::: {.callout-tip #divs-figs}
Citations inside figure captions ~~do not~~ work, we need to use [figure divs](https://quarto.org/docs/authoring/figures.html#figure-divs)
e.g. this is ~~no good~~ fine actually

````qmd
![See @Hall2022Can — the attention economy of road signs](/images/science.abm3427-fa.avif)
````

But this is fine:

````qmd
:::{#fig-hallcan2022}
![](/images/science.abm3427-fa.avif)

See @Hall2022Can — the attention economy of road signs
:::
````

**UPDATE: [maybe I was dreaming about that](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/discussions/8799). It seems to work now.
:::

::: {.callout-tip #divs-figs}
Corollary: `#fig-` is a magic prefix for IDs in Quarto, which means you cannot use it for anything else, or _that_ will turn into a figure.
:::

:::{.callout-tip}
## Python script dependencies

Python is a [packaging disaster](./python_packaging.qmd).
So, e.g. my image processing script for this blog is invoked as
```yaml
  post-render:
    - uv rn massage_header_img
```

To make them work in a continuous integration setting I found it wise to also wrap the scripts with a shell script.
:::
